content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have a question about my lighting setup. I use an astronomical clock to switch the lights on around 20:00 at sunset, but I want them to turn off at midnight using the weekly timer. How can I achieve this? I can't get it to work.
Is your setup like what I included in the attachment?
Yes, but with the astronomical clock, the light turns on during the day instead of in the evening.
Did you check my screenshot carefully? The AND-block has the output from the astronomical clock inverted.
I want the light to be off during the day, turn on at sunset, and turn off at midnight.
Set it up like my screenshot shows.
But then it seems to use only the weekly timer and not the astronomical clock.
You need to clarify what you want. Should either the astronomical clock or the weekly timer at 8:00 p.m. switch on the light, and the weekly timer turn it off at midnight? Is that correct?
No, I want only the astronomical clock to turn the light on at sunset, and the weekly timer to turn it off at midnight.
Try this...
The light doesn't turn off at the set off time.
Show us your program. Without seeing it, I can't give advice.
See the attachment. Do you notice the differences between my program and yours?
I think there's some misunderstanding. I want the light to go on at sunset and turn off at 23:00.
That was your latest request, and my program accomplishes this.
I'm not getting the RS block setup as you show in the screenshot.
You're inverting the S-input of the latching relay in your program.
Try this.
The light still doesn't turn off at 23:00.

I can only comment on my proposed solution, and it should work as expected. You haven't included anything for your network input at address V30.0, so I can't assess its impact. Remove the network input for testing and you'll see the light goes off at 23:00. Alternatively, you can run an online test before 23:00 and check the status of that input. If V30.0 is set at 23:00, the RS block output won't have any effect. If you're using VM memory, avoid overlapping addresses. If you're using the webserver, a button might just set V30.0 permanently. In that case, connect a low signal output with the same address in the program.
The only way the light stays on is if the network input with V30.0 is involved, and it looks like you don't want to share your whole program for troubleshooting.
Still can't get it to work.
That's not very helpful...
Yes, the light turns on at sunset, which is good. But it doesn't go off at 23:00.
Show us your full program. Upload it as a ZIP file to the forum.
You didn't make the changes I suggested. Check the image. Attached is a corrected version.
I tried it, but the lights are off in the evening. I want them to turn on at sunset and off at 23:00.
With my changes, it works correctly. I don't know what you did differently. For me, this topic is done. Maybe someone else can help you.
I did it like you suggested—copied and pasted—but it's just not working.
Can someone assist me?

@M111, can you explain how that's helpful? Whether I use a falling edge to set the latching relay or a wiping relay with a negated trigger—can you describe the advantage? I can't see your approach as the solution.
It works as expected. You can try simulating it.

Try out my suggestions in the simulation—they also work. The topic starter might have a different issue but can't explain it well. Can you clarify the difference between: using a falling edge from the astronomical clock, or negating the output and using a wiping relay to trigger the pulse relay?

Okay, here's what should happen: the pool lights turn on at sunset when it gets dark. They should turn off when we go to sleep, at 23:00. I tried your file, but then the lights don't turn on at sunset (or the relay closes).
Did you add invert logic to the B005 wiping timer? Did you set the clock accurately in your controller? Can you share a screenshot of your program?

I use the inverted output from the astro clock as input for the wiping timer to generate a pulse and activate the latching relay, which turns on the light. At 23:00, the weekly timer resets the relay and the light goes off.
@M111, did you read this thread fully? Have you tested my program? The topic starter hasn't shared the full program...
Yes, I tested your program, and it seems the latching relay stays activated all night. So, even when it's reset at 23:00, it's still set to 'on'.
What do you think—does using the falling edge in my approach make a difference? When the astronomical clock switches off, the relay should be set.
Then you must have tested a different program than I did. I don't think it's helpful to keep trying here, as another user with limited knowledge has joined in.
He may need to check the astronomical clock parameters too. My program works as intended.
Mine does too, so your program doesn't offer a better or more helpful solution.

Your method will always set the relay. So, even if you use the weekly timer to reset it, the astronomical clock can't turn on the light at night the next day. I tested my program and it works perfectly if the astronomical and real-time clocks are set correctly.
Why shouldn't the astronomical clock switch on the next day? I doubt you fully understand and tested my solution.

Sorry, I tested your approach again. Your NAND edge works like a wiping timer, and it functions properly. The sun rises and sets trigger the NAND edge for one cycle and activate the relay. Your program works well too.

You're not reading what I want. I need the light to be off during the day, turn ON at sunset, turn OFF at 23:00, and stay off the rest of the night and day. Then repeat: on at sunset, off at 23:00, etc.
That's what my program does. I don't know why it doesn't work for you. You say your program matches mine, but when you upload it, it's not the same as what I provided.
I already uploaded my program in that ZIP file. How do you want me to share it?
My program works as you describe. You can test it in actual operation.

Mine works too. I tried it on an actual controller. But the topic starter can't integrate it correctly. I made changes to his uploaded program and re-uploaded the corrected version. I don't know why you keep posting here—it's not helping.
Now the lights are on during the day.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are having difficulty configuring a lighting setup using both an astronomical clock and a weekly timer so the lights switch on at sunset and off at midnight. The main challenge is unclear logic and interactions between the two timers, causing confusion and conflicting advice. Many posts highlight the complexity of syncing these timing sources for precise control.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the astronomical clock to switch the light on automatically at sunset, and the weekly timer to ensure the light reliably turns off at midnight. They seek a seamless cooperation between both timers for consistent sequential automation.
